title: `uv add --index <name>=<url> <package>` can overwrite an index of the wrong format
author: EliteTK
body_preview: `uv add --index <name>=<url> <package>` will match pre-existing indexes on `<name>` and overwrite the `<url>`. This can break indexes with the wrong format, silently.  ```console $ uv init --bare --name test Initialized project `test` $ cat >> pyproject.toml <<EOF >  > [[tool.uv.index]] > name = "index" > url = "https://example.com/flat" > format = "flat" > EOF $ uv add iniconfig --index index=htt...

title: `uv add --index <name>=<url> <package>` can rename indexes used for source pins
author: EliteTK
body_preview: If you `uv add <package> --index <name>=<url>` and there is an existing index with `<url>` as its url, but with a different `<name>`, it will be renamed.  If there are packages with `[tool.uv.sources]` entries pointing at the old name, they will not be updated.  If you are not running with `--frozen` this will result in an error and a rollback. title: `uv add --index <name>=<url> <package>` can resolve differently to a subsequent `uv lock`
author: EliteTK
body_preview: If `<name>` is an implicit index in a `pyproject.toml`, `uv add --index <name>=<url> <package>` will update the index URL, pin the package, re-order the index to be at the top/first, and keep it implicit.
